paper: Dalvi et al. (2021). Explaining Answers with Entailment Trees. EMNLP 2021.
task_formulation: Given a hypothesis (question+answer pair), generate a multi-step entailment tree whose leaves are corpus facts and whose internal nodes are intermediate conclusions. Three task variants: (1) gold leaves only, (2) gold + distractor leaves, (3) full corpus retrieval.
method_summary: T5-based EntailmentWriter generating the whole tree in one shot. Evaluation via four metrics after Jaccard-based node alignment: Leaves (F1, AllCorrect), Steps (F1, AllCorrect), Intermediates (F1, AllCorrect), Overall-AllCorrect (=1 only if all three are perfect). Intermediate correctness uses BLEURT for textual similarity.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Four EntailmentBank dimensions on Task 2 (per NLProofS comparison table): Overall-AllCorrect ≈ 20.9%, Leaves-AllCorrect ≈ 35.6% for EntailmentWriter baseline. Steps-AllCorrect and Intermediates-AllCorrect are tracked but specific baseline numbers for EntailmentWriter not reported in report B.
dataset: EntailmentBank (~1,840 trees) built on ARC science questions + WorldTree V2 fact corpus.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: No evidence-quality metadata; leaves assumed true (no provenance, no retraction/invalidation); grounds only in curated closed-corpus science facts; issues answer/verdict rather than symmetric no-verdict presentation; termination = axiom-matching in corpus, not KB-grounding with per-premise confidence.

paper: Hong et al. (2022). METGEN: A Module-Based Entailment Tree Generation Framework for Answer Explanation. Findings of NAACL 2022.
task_formulation: Module-based stepwise entailment tree generation with a controller selecting reasoning-type modules; decomposes n-premise steps (n>2) into 2-premise steps for tractability.
method_summary: ALBERT-xxlarge controller selects from T5-large reasoning modules at each step. Uses EntailmentBank Leaves/Steps/Intermediates/Overall-AllCorrect metrics. Human expert validity check by three students per step/tree for qualitative validation.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Improves Steps F1 and Overall-AllCorrect over EntailmentWriter baseline on EntailmentBank; specific numbers not reported in report B.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Same closed-corpus grounding as EntailmentBank — leaves assumed true, no evidence-quality metadata, no invalidation propagation; verdict-issuing.
derivation: extractor-inferred for metrics (report B does not give specific METGEN numbers)

paper: Ribeiro et al. (2022). Entailment Tree Explanations via Iterative Retrieval-Generation Reasoner (IRGR). NAACL 2022.
task_formulation: Iterative Retrieval-Generation Reasoner alternating retrieval of premises with step generation on EntailmentBank; same four EntailmentBank metrics.
method_summary: IRGR iterates between premise retrieval and entailment-step generation rather than generating the whole tree in one shot. Evaluated with the standard EntailmentBank four-metric suite.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Competitive with EntailmentWriter; specific numbers not reported in report B.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: No per-premise quality metadata; no contested-claim handling; closed corpus with assumed-true leaves; no invalidation.

paper: Liu et al. (2022). RLET: A Reinforcement Learning Based Approach for Explainable QA with Entailment Trees. EMNLP 2022.
task_formulation: Reinforcement-learning entailment tree construction over EntailmentBank, with reward signals for correct step structure.
method_summary: RL-based controller constructs trees incrementally, rewarding steps that match gold EntailmentBank annotations. Uses the same four-metric evaluation suite.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Improvements on EntailmentBank; specific numbers not reported in report B.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Closed corpus; no evidence-quality metadata; leaves assumed true; verdict-issuing; no invalidation.

paper: Yang, Deng & Chen (2022). NLProofS: Verifier-Guided Stepwise Search for Logical Proof. EMNLP 2022.
task_formulation: Verifier-guided stepwise proof search on EntailmentBank: a learned verifier scores candidate proof steps to control search and reduce hallucinated steps.
method_summary: Learned verifier judges entailment validity of generated steps; verifier-guided beam search raises step correctness without requiring larger generators. Evaluated with EntailmentBank four-metric suite.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Task 2 Overall-AllCorrect: 20.9% → 33.3%; Leaves-AllCorrect: 35.6% → 58.8% vs. T5-11B EntailmentWriter using only T5-large.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Verifier judges entailment validity of steps, not evidence quality of leaf facts; no provenance/invalidation; closed corpus; verdict-issuing.

paper: Kazemi et al. (2023). LAMBADA: Backward Chaining for Automated Reasoning in Natural Language. ACL 2023.
task_formulation: Logical reasoning over natural-language rule bases via backward chaining; decides if a goal is provable and produces the derivation proof. The closest published analog to Verity's recursive premise decomposition.
method_summary: Backward chaining decomposed into four LM-prompted sub-modules (Fact Check, Rule Selection, Goal Decomposition, Sign Agreement); large gains over Chain-of-Thought and Selection-Inference at depth; ~11.8× fewer inference calls than SI at Depth-5.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Label accuracy + proof accuracy on ProofWriter Depth-5; ~11.8× fewer inference calls than Selection-Inference at Depth-5.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Operates over given synthetic axioms (closed-world toy rule bases), not retrieved real-world evidence; termination = axiom/fact match in the provided theory; no evidence-quality metadata; produces proved/disproved verdict rather than symmetric no-verdict output.

paper: Tafjord, Dalvi & Clark (2021). ProofWriter: Generating Implications, Proofs, and Abductive Statements over Natural Language. Findings of ACL-IJCNLP 2021.
task_formulation: T5 generative model producing implications and proofs over natural-language theories; iterating a 1-step generator yields reliable proofs; supports abduction (inferring minimal missing facts).
method_summary: T5 trained over RuleTaker/ParaRules generates implications + proofs in one shot; iterative application generalizes to unseen depths.
metrics_and_best_numbers: +9% proof accuracy over PRover baseline; generalizes to unseen depths.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Synthetic closed-world theories; no evidence grounding or quality metadata; verdict-issuing; no invalidation.

paper: Tafjord, Dalvi Mishra & Clark (2022). Entailer: Answering Questions with Faithful and Truthful Chains of Reasoning. EMNLP 2022.
task_formulation: Answers questions with faithful chains of reasoning by generating and self-verifying proofs grounded in the model's own parametric beliefs.
method_summary: Model generates a proof chain and self-verifies each step against its own parametric knowledge rather than an external provenance-tracked KB.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Not specified in report B.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Grounds in model parametric belief rather than an external provenance-tracked KB; no evidence-quality layer; produces answers/verdicts; no invalidation propagation.
derivation: extractor-inferred (no external URL for Entailer in sources_b.md; description from report B text only)

paper: Weir, Clark & Van Durme (2024). NELLIE: A Neuro-Symbolic Inference Engine for Grounded, Compositional, and Explainable Reasoning. IJCAI 2024.
task_formulation: Grounded, compositional QA as entailment-tree proof search over an NL corpus of authoritative facts using Prolog-style backward-chaining inference with an LLM dynamic rule generator.
method_summary: Prolog-style backward chaining: handcrafted rules replaced by LLM dynamic rule generator + guided generation + semiparametric dense retrieval; recursively decomposes a hypothesis into subqueries proved from a knowledge store or recursively further decomposed.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Outperforms similar-sized SOTA reasoner (Entailer/Tafjord 2022) on QA accuracy and grounded-explanation quality on EntailmentBank + science QA datasets.
dataset: EntailmentBank + science QA (both semi-structured and NL corpora)
not_handled_relative_to_verity: No evidence-quality metadata (study design, retraction, source diversity); no invalidation propagation; issues an answer rather than symmetric no-verdict output; corpus is 'authoritative facts', not contested real-world claims with contrasting evidence. Architecturally closest system to Verity's recursive decomposition + KB grounding, but missing all three of Verity's distinctive layers.

paper: Min et al. (2023). FActScore: Fine-Grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation. EMNLP 2023.
task_formulation: Breaks a long-form generation into atomic facts and computes the percentage of atomic facts supported by a reliable knowledge source (Wikipedia). Introduces an automated estimator that closely tracks human annotation.
method_summary: LLM-based decomposition into atomic facts + retrieval against Wikipedia; automated estimator achieves <2% error vs. human annotators; human inter-annotator agreement >88% across three models tested.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Human inter-annotator agreement: 96%/90%/88% (InstructGPT/ChatGPT/PerplexityAI outputs); automated estimator <2% error vs. humans; ChatGPT biography factuality ~58%.
dataset: 549 biography prompts across InstructGPT, ChatGPT, PerplexityAI outputs.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: No recursive premise entailment (flat independent atomic facts); binary supported/unsupported (no evidence-quality gradient, no study design or retraction metadata); single-source grounding (Wikipedia); no invalidation; no symmetric contested-claim treatment.

paper: Wei et al. (2024). Long-form Factuality in Large Language Models (SAFE). NeurIPS 2024.
task_formulation: Decomposes long-form LLM output into atomic self-contained facts; per-fact multi-step agentic Google Search + reasoning; rates each fact supported/not-supported/irrelevant; computes F1@K over a LongFact prompt set.
method_summary: Three-stage pipeline: decompose → agentic multi-step Google Search per fact → LLM reasoning for verdict (supported/not-supported/irrelevant). >20× cheaper than human annotation; SAFE agrees with crowd humans 72% on ~16k facts and wins 76% of disagreement cases.
metrics_and_best_numbers: SAFE agrees with crowd humans 72% on ~16,000 facts; wins 76% of 100 manually reviewed disagreement cases; >20× cheaper per fact than human annotation.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Dynamic web references only (no persistent provenance-tracked KB, no invalidation); no evidence-quality metadata beyond supported/unsupported; no recursive entailment structure; no symmetric contested-claim treatment.

paper: Song, Kim & Iyyer (2024). VeriScore: Evaluating the Factuality of Verifiable Claims in Long-form Text Generation. Findings of EMNLP 2024.
task_formulation: Extracts only verifiable claims from long-form text (rejecting the FActScore/SAFE assumption that all claims are verifiable); uses inter-sentence context for self-contained decontextualized claims; retrieve + verify.
method_summary: Claim extraction filter identifies verifiable vs. non-verifiable claims; retrieval + classification as supported/unsupported/inconclusive; F1 combining precision + recall over 8 diverse tasks.
metrics_and_best_numbers: F1 combining precision + recall on 8 tasks; specific numbers not reported in report B.
dataset: 8 diverse tasks (task names not specified in report B)
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Still flat verifiable-claim extraction (no premise-entailment recursion); no evidence-quality bias graph; no invalidation; no contested-claim symmetry.
derivation: extractor-inferred for metrics (report B does not give specific VeriScore numbers)

paper: Wanner, Ebner, Jiang, Dredze & Van Durme (2024). A Closer Look at Claim Decomposition. *SEM 2024.
task_formulation: Empirical study showing FActScore is sensitive to the decomposition method — error can arise from the decomposer, not just the generator. Introduces DecompScore to measure decomposition quality without a gold standard.
method_summary: DecompScore (adaptation of FActScore measuring decomposition quality); Russellian/neo-Davidsonian LLM decomposition improving quality. Core finding: decomposition quality has no gold standard — measured by number of supported subclaims / entailment-coverage proxy.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Demonstrates FActScore error attributable to decomposer; DecompScore quantifies decomposition quality via proxy. Specific numeric improvements not reported in report B.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Still Wikipedia-grounded; no entailment structure linking premises to a composite claim; no evidence-quality metadata; directly establishes the proxy-only status (Bucket 2) for Verity's decomposition faithfulness evaluation.

paper: Wanner, Van Durme & Dredze (2025). DnDScore: Decontextualization and Decomposition for Factuality Verification. EMNLP 2025.
task_formulation: Studies the tension between decomposition (isolating atomic facts) and decontextualization (re-inserting context so subclaims are verifiable); finds strategy choice materially changes factuality scores.
method_summary: Systematic comparison of decomposition and decontextualization strategies and their effect on downstream factuality scores. Related to Molecular Facts (Gunjal & Durrett 2024), CORE (Jiang et al. 2024), WiCE (Kamoi et al. 2023).
metrics_and_best_numbers: Factuality score instability across strategies demonstrated; specific numeric results not reported in report B.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Measures verification-score stability from decomposition strategy choices, not per-premise evidence quality; no invalidation; no contested-claim symmetry.
derivation: extractor-inferred for dataset and specific metrics

paper: Thorne et al. (2018). FEVER: A Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification. NAACL 2018.
task_formulation: 185k claims derived from Wikipedia, annotated as Supported/Refuted/NotEnoughInfo; systems must retrieve evidence sentences AND produce correct label; FEVER score credits verdict only when correct evidence is retrieved.
method_summary: TF-IDF/BM25 baselines → dense retrieval → LLM query generation across five FEVER shared-task workshops. Dominant evaluation paradigm for evidence-retrieval + verdict classification.
metrics_and_best_numbers: FEVER score (label correct AND evidence retrieved correctly); specific system numbers vary across workshops; benchmark evolves through FEVER 1–5 shared tasks.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Single-source closed corpus (Wikipedia); no evidence-quality metadata; verdict-issuing; no premise entailment tree; no invalidation.
derivation: extractor-inferred (FEVER NAACL 2018 primary URL not verified in sources_b.md; sources_a.md entry labeled '(FEVER)' at aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.609 is likely a mislabeling — EMNLP 2020 is SciFact's venue, not FEVER's; see EXTRACTION_NOTES)

paper: Wadden et al. (2020). Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims (SciFact). EMNLP 2020.
task_formulation: 1,409 expert-written biomedical claims derived from citances; pipeline: abstract retrieval → rationale sentence selection → SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NOINFO label prediction. SciFact-Open (2022) expands to 500K abstracts.
method_summary: Abstract-level retrieval followed by rationale (evidence sentence) selection and label prediction; expert annotators write claims against a corpus of 5,183 biomedical abstracts.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Abstract-retrieval recall, rationale-selection F1, label accuracy; SciFact-Open extends corpus to 500K abstracts.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Rationale = evidence sentences, not study-design/sample-size/retraction metadata; no per-premise recursion; verdict-issuing; no invalidation.

paper: Schlichtkrull et al. (2023). AVeriTeC: A Dataset for Real-world Claim Verification with Evidence from the Web. EMNLP 2023 (Datasets & Benchmarks).
task_formulation: 4,568 real-world fact-checked claims from 50 organizations; QA-pair evidence from the web; four labels: Supported/Refuted/Not Enough Evidence/Conflicting Evidence & Cherry-picking. AVeriTeC score = fraction with correct label AND evidence quality above threshold.
method_summary: QA-pair evidence generation for each claim; AVeriTeC score metric: fraction of claims with correct label AND evidence quality above Hungarian METEOR ≥0.25 (2024) or Ev2R recall threshold (2025). 2024 shared task: 21 submissions, winner TUDA_MAI scored 63%; Conflicting/Cherry-picking is the hardest class (near-zero F1, <7% training data).
metrics_and_best_numbers: 2024 shared task (Hungarian METEOR): TUDA_MAI 63%, AIC CTU 50.4%, baseline 0.202. 2025 (Ev2R metric): CTU AIC 0.332, HerO2 0.271, baseline 0.202. Conflicting/Cherry-picking class near-zero F1 for most systems.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: The Conflicting/Cherry-picking label is the closest existing analog to Verity's contested-claim stance, but it is still a verdict (fifth category), not symmetric no-verdict presentation; no evidence-quality metadata per premise (study design/retraction); no recursive entailment tree; no KB invalidation. Note: 2024 and 2025 metric scores are not comparable (different metric formulas).

paper: Nakshatri et al. (2025). Talking Point based Ideological Discourse Analysis in News Events. Findings of ACL 2025.
task_formulation: Analyze ideological discourse in news events via relational talking points (entities, roles, media frames, topic); build vocabulary of prominent talking points across publications; generate ideology-specific partisan perspectives per news event.
method_summary: Theory-driven ideological discourse analysis framework layering LLM extraction + PTP (Prominent Talking Point) clustering over news events; validation by downstream ideology classification accuracy + partisan classification at PTP-cluster level + human assessments and automated evaluations.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Ideology classification (left/right prediction for unseen articles using generated perspectives) + partisan classification at PTP-cluster level; 'correlation was really high' vs. expert PhD raters on human validation.
dataset: KeyEvents (Nakshatri et al. 2023) sampled from NELA-2021
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Characterizes ideological perspectives, not per-premise evidence quality; no entailment grounding; no KB provenance/invalidation. Validation approach — downstream classification + sampled human agreement — is a direct template for Verity's decomposition and bias-graph validation.

paper: Watts et al. (2024). Penn Media Bias Detector / CSSLab PennMAP. Launched June 2024.
task_formulation: Scrapes 10 major US online newspapers 4×/day; GPT-4 classifies article topic/subtopic, tone, and political lean; tracks events via sliding-window semantic similarity; explicitly refuses to score bias against 'truth' — compares outlets to each other.
method_summary: GPT-4 labeling with human-in-the-loop RA audits (random sample monitoring); construct validity checked vs. expert PhD raters ('correlation was really high'; GPT-4 sometimes outperforms humans on some tasks); no-verdict philosophy ('you can't really measure bias directly').
metrics_and_best_numbers: Comparison to PhD expert raters: 'correlation was really high'; GPT-4 outperforms humans on some tasks. Specific correlation coefficients not reported in report B.
dataset: 10 major US online newspapers (planned expansion to 22 by January 2026); 4 scrapes/day, sliding-window event clustering.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: No premise entailment; no evidence-quality metadata on sources; no KB invalidation; validated by sampled human agreement, not benchmark. The symmetric no-verdict philosophy ('our goal is not to adjudicate what is true') is a direct precedent for Verity's transparency-only stance.
derivation: extractor-inferred for specific metrics (specific correlation numbers not in report B)

paper: Costello, Pennycook & Rand (2024). Durably reducing conspiracy beliefs through dialogues with AI. Science 385(6714):eadq1814.
task_formulation: GPT-4 Turbo engages 2,190 conspiracy believers in personalized, evidence-based dialogues; measures belief change immediately and at 2-month follow-up; tests generalization across conspiracy theory types.
method_summary: Two experiments; GPT-4 Turbo generates personalized counter-arguments with evidence; ~20% reduction in conspiracy belief, durable at 2 months, generalizes across theories, holds even for deeply entrenched believers. AAAS Newcomb Cleveland Prize 2026. Subject to Science Editorial Expression of Concern (June 11, 2026) over data-reproducibility and screening-criteria inconsistencies between experiments.
metrics_and_best_numbers: ~20% reduction in conspiracy belief; effect durable at 2 months; generalizes across wide range of theories; 192 citations (Clarivate). Effect sizes materially weakened by the June 2026 Editorial Expression of Concern — treat as upper-bound estimates pending correction.
dataset: 2,190 conspiracy believers across 2 experiments (online panel, Prolific/CloudResearch-style)
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Measures persuasion/attitude change, not decomposition or verification quality; AI issues persuasive verdicts (opposite of Verity's no-verdict stance); relevant only as motivational background that facts+evidence can move beliefs. The June 2026 EoC means this paper should not be cited without pairing with independent replications (Boissin et al. PNAS Nexus 2025, 'Just the facts' OSF 2025).

paper: Costello, Pennycook & Rand (2025). Just the facts: How dialogues with AI reduce conspiracy beliefs. OSF Preprint.
task_formulation: Mechanism study of DebunkBot effect: 8 treatment arms testing whether facts/evidence or framing drives the belief-reduction effect (told AI aims to persuade, asked to debate, asked for concise responses).
method_summary: N≈1,297 online panel; 8 within-subjects arms; effect robust across all framing manipulations, supporting facts/evidence (not framing) as the active mechanism.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Belief reduction robust across all 8 framing conditions (N≈1,297); supports 'facts/evidence, not framing' as mechanism.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Confirms facts move beliefs but Verity deliberately withholds verdicts; motivation not component evaluation. Unpublished preprint as of report date.

paper: Boissin, Costello, Spinoza-Martín, Rand & Pennycook (2025). Dialogues with large language models reduce conspiracy beliefs even when the AI is perceived as human. PNAS Nexus 4(11):pgaf325.
task_formulation: Pre-registered RCT testing whether belief reduction holds when participants think they are talking to a human rather than an AI; isolates message from messenger.
method_summary: N=955 pre-registered; conditions vary participant belief about whether they are talking to AI or human; message (factual evidence) drives effect regardless of perceived messenger identity.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Effect holds regardless of human/AI perception (N=955, pre-registered); messenger identity does not moderate effect.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Corroborates Costello et al. 2024 direction despite the EoC; motivation not component evaluation. Messenger-irrelevance finding is independent replication value for Verity's motivation section.
derivation: extractor-inferred (PNAS Nexus URL not provided in sources_b.md; description from report B text only)

paper: Anonymous (2025). Dialogues with AI Reduce Beliefs in Misinformation but Build No Lasting Discernment Skills. arXiv:2510.01537.
task_formulation: Tests whether AI-dialogue-induced belief shifts transfer to lasting discernment skills (ability to independently detect misinformation on new stimuli).
method_summary: Skill-transfer study measuring discernment after AI dialogue intervention; finding: belief shifts do not transfer to independent discernment skills.
metrics_and_best_numbers: No significant skill transfer to discernment on new stimuli (specific n not reported in report B).
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Directly relevant to Verity's evaluation design: Verity should measure calibration/discernment (not persuasion), since Verity deliberately does not persuade. The skill-transfer critique implies measuring attitude change is insufficient to validate Verity's transparency-only approach.
derivation: extractor-inferred for dataset and specific numbers; arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed as of report date

paper: Anonymous (2026). Large language models can effectively convince people to believe conspiracies. arXiv:2601.05050.
task_formulation: Demonstrates that the same LLM persuasion machinery used to reduce conspiracy beliefs can be repurposed to increase conspiracy beliefs — dual-use caution for evidence-based dialogue systems.
method_summary: Uses the same persuasion architecture as DebunkBot in the belief-amplifying direction; quantifies effectiveness of LLM-driven conspiracy promotion.
metrics_and_best_numbers: LLMs effectively increase conspiracy beliefs (specific magnitude not reported in report B).
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Caution for any system that issues verdicts or persuasive content; Verity's no-verdict design mitigates this risk by design. Not a component evaluation.
derivation: extractor-inferred for dataset and metrics; arXiv preprint, 2026, not peer-reviewed as of report date

paper: Carlson et al. (2010) / Mitchell et al. (2018). Never-Ending Language Learning (NELL). AAAI 2010 / CACM 61(5):103–115.
task_formulation: Architecture for never-ending language learning: continuously extracts beliefs from the web via coupled semi-supervised learning across four components (CPL, CSEAL, CMC, RL) unified by a Knowledge Integrator; maintains a persistent growing KB with provenance and belief promotion/demotion.
method_summary: EM-like loop: candidate beliefs promoted when supported by high-confidence source(s) or multiple independent sources (posterior threshold ≥0.75/0.9); Knowledge Integrator (ErrorBasedIntegrator) demotes/deletes beliefs via consistency/coupling violations; ~10-15 min/day human oversight approving rules. Ran to iteration 1115 (Sept 3, 2018).
metrics_and_best_numbers: ~1.78M concepts, 623 relations, ~2.2M beliefs by iteration 905; acknowledged semantic drift (incorrect beliefs accumulate) mitigated but not solved by coupling constraints.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: No evidence-quality metadata in the fact-checking sense (no study design, retraction status); no claim-level dependency-propagated invalidation. Key lesson for Verity: provenance-tagged promotion + coupling constraints are the KB pattern needed; semantic drift is the central risk of a persistent verified-fact KB.

paper: Doyle (1979). A Truth Maintenance System. Artificial Intelligence 12(3):231–272.
task_formulation: Formal dependency-directed belief maintenance: nodes carry justifications; belief status labeled IN/OUT; dependency-directed backtracking traces contradictions to responsible assumptions and retracts precisely those. Upstream premise retraction automatically makes dependent conclusions OUT.
method_summary: JTMS: justification-based nodes; IN/OUT propagation automatically maintains consistent belief set; when a leaf fact is retracted, all dependent conclusions propagate OUT via dependency graph — the direct formal model for Verity's premise invalidation propagation.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Formal system; no empirical benchmarks.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Foundational formalism only; not applied to scholarly retractions or real-world fact-checking claims; no evidence-quality metadata; single consistent context (vs. ATMS's multiple contexts). JTMS is the direct formal model for Verity's dependency-invalidation layer.
derivation: extractor-inferred (1979 journal paper; no direct URL in sources_b.md; described from report B text)

paper: de Kleer (1986). An Assumption-based TMS / Extending the ATMS / Problem Solving with the ATMS. Artificial Intelligence 28(2):127–262.
task_formulation: Assumption-based TMS (ATMS): tracks assumptions, environments (minimal assumption sets), nogoods (inconsistent environments), and labels (minimal consistent environments per node); enables simultaneous multiple contexts — context switching is free, most backtracking avoided.
method_summary: ATMS: invalidating an assumption marks all environments containing it as nogood; conclusions lose validity only in those environments, preserving valid contexts. 'Context switching is free and most backtracking (and all retraction) is avoided.'
metrics_and_best_numbers: Formal system; no empirical benchmarks.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Foundational formalism only; not applied to scholarly retractions or fact-checking. ATMS is the model for Verity if it must hold multiple evidential contexts simultaneously (e.g., contested claims with incompatible evidence streams) without committing to one.
derivation: extractor-inferred (1986 journal paper; no primary URL in sources_b.md; described from report B text)

paper: Nicholson et al. (2021). scite: A smart citation index that displays the context of citations and classifies their intent using deep learning. Quantitative Science Studies 2(3):882–898.
task_formulation: Smart citation index classifying citation statements as Supporting, Contrasting(Disputing), or Mentioning via a SciBERT deep-learning classifier; measures the distribution and reliability of citation intent classification at scale.
method_summary: SciBERT classifier trained on citation statements; highly imbalanced class distribution (92.6% mentioning, 6.5% supporting, 0.8% contrasting); production per-class precision >80% (vendor figure); independent 2023 Hypothesis journal evaluation found heavy over-labeling as 'mentioning' on a retracted-paper sample. API is commercial only.
metrics_and_best_numbers: Production precision >80% per class (vendor-reported); 880M classified citation statements at 2021 publication; 1.6B+ Smart Citations / 300M+ articles currently. Independent 2023 evaluation disputes accuracy (over-labeling as 'mentioning').
dataset: 880M+ full-text citation statements at publication time; 300M+ articles indexed.
not_handled_relative_to_verity: Citation-level, not premise-level; no recursive decomposition; no claim-level invalidation; API is commercial (no free public tier); coarse 3-class intent insufficient for Verity's evidence-quality layer. Sample-size metadata is explicitly called 'exceedingly difficult' to classify by the authors themselves (verbatim in paper).
